questions.topic: Top two per group with a tie
questions.learningObjective: Select top two per group with ties
questions.stem: A historical case needs the top 2 sales per region including ties. Which function helps?

options.misconception: excludes ties beyond the first two

questions.explanation: RANK or DENSE_RANK with a filter <= 2 includes tied rows beyond the first two. ROW_NUMBER would arbitrarily cut ties.

questions.topic: Rows a recursive walk produces
questions.stem: A historical case recursive CTE walks a 3-level org chart with 1 root, 2 children, and 4 grandchildren. How many rows result?
questions.explanation: The anchor seeds the root and recursion expands to children and grandchildren, totaling 1 plus 2 plus 4 equals 7 rows.

questions.topic: Which queries a composite index can seek
questions.stem: A historical case has a composite index on (last_name, first_name). Can a query filtering only first_name seek the index?

answer.exemplar: No, because the leading column last_name is missing, so the index cannot be seeked efficiently from first_name alone.

questions.explanation: Composite indexes are seekable from the leading column. Skipping the leading column prevents an efficient seek.

questions.topic: Inner rows a nested-loop join reads
questions.stem: A historical case nested-loop join reads 5 outer rows and 4 inner rows per outer. How many inner reads occur?
questions.explanation: Each outer row triggers a scan of the inner table, so 5 times 4 equals 20 inner reads.

questions.topic: Rows produced by a lost join condition
questions.learningObjective: Predict cartesian product from missing join
questions.stem: A historical case query omits the join condition between 3 customers and 4 orders. How many rows result?

options.text: Zero, because no join means no rows

questions.explanation: Without a join condition, every customer pairs with every order: 3 times 4 equals 12 rows.

questions.topic: Rows an offset page repeats
questions.stem: A historical case paginates with OFFSET 10 LIMIT 10. If a new row is inserted before page 2, what happens?

options.text: A row from page 1 may repeat on page 2

questions.explanation: Inserting a row shifts subsequent rows, so an offset-based page can repeat or skip rows.

questions.topic: Queries a repeated lookup issues
questions.stem: A historical case loads 20 orders and then queries items for each order. How many queries issue?

options.text: Twenty-one, one for orders plus twenty for items

questions.explanation: The N+1 problem issues one query for the parent rows plus one per parent, totaling 21 queries.

questions.topic: Distinct entities behind duplicated links
questions.stem: A historical case has 8 links but only 5 distinct entities. Why does COUNT(*) differ from COUNT(DISTINCT entity)?

answer.exemplar: COUNT(*) counts every link including duplicates, while COUNT(DISTINCT entity) counts each entity once, so duplicates inflate the first count.

questions.explanation: Duplicated links inflate row counts. Distinct counting removes duplicate entities.

questions.topic: Top two per group with a tie
questions.learningObjective: Count rows for top two with tie
questions.stem: A historical case group has sales 10,9,9,8. Top 2 by RANK returns how many rows?
questions.explanation: RANK assigns 1 to 10 and 2 to both 9s, so filtering rank <= 2 returns 3 rows.

questions.topic: Rows a recursive walk produces
questions.stem: A historical case recursive CTE stops when no new rows are found. What is this state called?
questions.explanation: Recursion ends at a fixed point when a pass adds no new rows.

questions.topic: Which queries a composite index can seek
questions.stem: A historical case has index on (city, age). Which query can seek efficiently?

options.misconception: reorders but still seeks via city

questions.explanation: A seek requires the leading column city. City equality is seekable; age-only is not.

questions.topic: Inner rows a nested-loop join reads
questions.stem: A historical case nested-loop join reads 10 outer and 10 inner rows per outer. What is the total inner reads?
questions.explanation: Each outer row scans the inner table, so 10 times 10 equals 100 reads.

questions.topic: Rows produced by a lost join condition
questions.stem: A historical case query forgets the ON clause. Why does the result explode?

answer.exemplar: Without a join condition, every row from one table pairs with every row from the other, producing a cartesian product.

questions.explanation: The missing condition removes the filter, so all combinations appear in the output.

questions.topic: Rows an offset page repeats
questions.stem: A historical case page size is 10 and offset is 10. If 2 rows are inserted before page 2, how many original page-2 rows repeat?
questions.explanation: Two inserted rows push two original rows into the next page, causing two repeats.

questions.topic: Queries a repeated lookup issues
questions.stem: A historical case loads 50 users and queries orders per user. What is this pattern called?

options.misconception: confuses repeated queries with cross product
confuses query count with scan type

questions.explanation: Issuing one query per parent row is the N+1 problem. It can be fixed with a join or batch loading.

questions.topic: Distinct entities behind duplicated links

questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts every row including duplicates, so it returns 12.

questions.topic: Top two per group with a tie

questions.stem: A historical case wants exactly 2 rows per group regardless of ties. Which function fits?
questions.explanation: ROW_NUMBER assigns unique positions, so filtering <= 2 yields exactly 2 rows per group even with ties.

questions.topic: Rows a recursive walk produces
questions.stem: A historical case recursive CTE walks a 2-level tree with 1 root and 3 children. How many rows result?

answer.exemplar: The recursive walk produces 4 rows because the anchor contributes the root and recursion adds the 3 children.

questions.explanation: Anchor plus recursive expansion yields 1 plus 3 equals 4 rows.

questions.topic: Which queries a composite index can seek
questions.stem: A historical case composite index has 3 columns. How many leading columns must be present for a full seek?
questions.explanation: A full composite seek uses all columns in order, so all 3 leading columns are needed for the most specific seek.

questions.topic: Inner rows a nested-loop join reads

options.text: The join becomes a hash join
options.misconception: confuses index seek with hash join

options.text: The outer table is no longer read
Each outer row seeks the inner index instead of scanning

questions.explanation: An index on the inner table turns per-outer scans into seeks, reducing reads.

questions.topic: Rows produced by a lost join condition

questions.topic: Rows an offset page repeats
questions.stem: A historical case uses OFFSET for pagination. Why can rows be skipped or repeated?

options.text: Because offset is position-based and data changes

questions.explanation: Offset pagination relies on row positions, which shift when data changes, causing skips or repeats.

questions.topic: Queries a repeated lookup issues
questions.stem: A historical case loads 10 authors and queries books per author. How many queries issue?

answer.exemplar: Eleven queries issue because one loads the authors and ten more load books for each author.

questions.explanation: The N+1 pattern issues 1 plus N queries. Here N is 10, so 11 total.

questions.topic: Distinct entities behind duplicated links
questions.stem: A historical case has 15 links and 9 distinct entities. How many duplicate links exist?
questions.explanation: Subtract distinct entities from total links: 15 minus 9 equals 6 duplicate links.

questions.topic: Top two per group with a tie

options.text: RANK includes tied rows in the top two

questions.explanation: RANK ties equal values, so filtering <= 2 includes all tied rows. ROW_NUMBER cuts ties arbitrarily.

questions.topic: Rows a recursive walk produces
questions.stem: A historical case recursive CTE has a cycle in the data. What is the risk?
questions.explanation: A cycle causes the recursive member to keep producing rows until a limit or cycle guard stops it.

questions.topic: Which queries a composite index can seek
questions.stem: A historical case index on (a,b) is queried with WHERE a = 1 AND b > 2. Can it seek?

options.text: No, because b is a range
Yes, leading column a is equality and b is range

questions.explanation: A composite index seeks on leading equality a and then ranges on b, which is efficient.

options.text: Yes, if the index is unique
No, because LIKE is never indexed

questions.explanation: A leading wildcard prevents index seek because the starting position is unknown. A trailing wildcard allows seek.
